picks.title: Nobody asked for the sparkle button
picks.excerpt: Products ship with the same AI sparkle panel while people hunt for the off switch and spend outruns returns; the author argues teams should build features with AI, not AI features.
picks.rationale: A sharp product-design argument against bolt-on AI sparkle panels that gives teams a test to apply to their own roadmap: build features with AI, not AI features. It is a different thesis from earlier UXC pieces in the history.

picks.title: Where to draw the line before AI reaches professional users
picks.excerpt: Every B2B roadmap now has a chat box; six questions for deciding whether a conversational layer speeds experts up or puts a keyboard between them and work they already know.
picks.rationale: Swap-in #2 for the Epic game-jam card. It gives B2B product designers a six-question checklist for deciding whether a chat layer helps expert users or slows them down, which they can apply to a roadmap tomorrow. It is a different thesis from the 10-12 Tesler's-law piece and the 10-08 bounded-delegation piece. This is the third figma-category card (cap relaxed to 3 for this swap) and gets the palette accent #7928ca.

picks.title: Why do AI platforms want humans to design their branding?
picks.excerpt: AI firms keep hiring human designers and agencies for their own brand identities, a telling irony for the creative industry.
picks.rationale: Points out that AI companies still hire human studios for their own brand identities, which is useful context for brand designers pitching against generative tools. It is a different story from the 09-28 NASA-brand piece. The second figma-category pick gets the palette accent #eb367f.

picks.title: Impeccable: The Open-Source Design Skill That Stops AI Websites Looking AI-Generated
picks.excerpt: Impeccable is an open-source design skill for AI coding agents that targets the tells of AI-built sites (Inter everywhere, purple gradients, nested cards) and pushes output toward deliberate visual design.
picks.rationale: A specific open-source agent skill that designers can install tomorrow to steer coding agents away from default AI styling. It is a different tool from the 10-22 haoli de-slop skill, which was the author's own project.
